title: Experiment: the compatibility contract re-proved from a real clean consumer, both platforms

facts.piInstalledBy: the consumer's own npm install into .planning/node_modules
facts.inference: local deterministic fake provider on 127.0.0.1, explicitly selected per run

summary: The first fixture was not a clean consumer and this replaces it. It now generates a temporary directory, runs `git init` and leaves the repository UNBORN with no commits, copies the tool from `git ls-files` so an uncommitted local file cannot make a run pass, runs the consumer's own `npm install` inside `.planning`, and resolves the CLI through the COPIED tool's installed package metadata via its `bin.pi` field. OBSERVED ON BOTH PLATFORMS: the resolved CLI reports 0.84.4, matches the pin read from this repository's manifest, lies inside the consumer directory, and does NOT lie inside the development checkout — the last being the assertion the previous fixture could not make, because it executed this repository's own node_modules. Every earlier finding reproduced against the new fixture: the five trust rows, the default active set of read/bash/edit/write, `--tools` narrowing, the relative package entry differing only by separator, three session-relocation routes, the task sentinel reaching the provider with stdin closed, skill-override precedence with its removal control, and the canary challenge arriving intact with prose and exclusion controls both empty.
notes: ⚠️ THE ENVIRONMENT IS NOW BUILT FROM AN ALLOWLIST, WHICH IS A SAFETY FIX AND NOT A TIDY-UP. The earlier scripts inherited all of `process.env` and ran Pi without naming a model. PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR isolates the stored auth file and does nothing whatever about environment authentication, so on a host carrying OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY a reproduction could have reached a paid provider. Two defences now: an allowlist of OS and runtime names that contains no credential, and an explicit loopback `--model` on every run that can reach inference. ⚠️ IT ALSO STOPPED BEING ONE PERSON'S SCRIPT — the old fixture hard-coded a developer's scratch path and nobody else could run it.
